newsitem.title: USA: IVC slowed by disappointing Revlon sales.
newsitem.headline: IVC slowed by disappointing Revlon sales.

text.p: IVC Industries Inc Wednesday reported an 8.3 percent decline in third quarter, April 30, sales citing a decision to drop a private brand program and continued disappointing Revlon vitamin sales.
Sales for the quarter were $25.4 million. The company had a profit of $337,000 compared to a a net loss in 1996 of $1,256,000 after pretax merger costs of $2,965,000.

"We believe our top-line growth will be driven through focusing on our branded/higher-margined product lines and direct-to-the-consumer distribution channels," I. Alan Hirschfeld, executive vice president, said.
"While we are continually seeking out private brand opportunities ... we anticipate doing so only when acceptable rates of returns can be realized."

IVC has determined the demands relative to some of these programs are no longer providing acceptable returns, it said. This was the case with one supply agreement which ended in late calendar 1996, and was not renewed.
Although overall sales wre hurt by the termination of that program, results are beginning to reflect the improvement in gross profit margins and overall profitability, said Hirschfeld.

The company said both sales and gross profit margins during the 1997 quarter were hurt by continued disappointing sales levels of its Revlon product line, especially when compared to the year ago quarter, when the line was launched.

Sales of the company's flagship brand, Fields of Nature, have been accelerating during the current year and especially during the third quarter, it continued. The company said branded products accounted for 25 percent of sales during the latest quarter, compared to 14 percent a year ago.

"This growth in branded sales, coupled with increasing national store penetration, has continued in the fourth quarter, and we are planning for further acceleration into next year and beyond," added Hirschfeld. "This top-line growth of our brands, along with the accompanying profit margin, augurs well for our overall profitability."
The company said it is also actively seeking to accelerate direct-to-the-consumer sales, including mail order, retail stores and multi-level distribution opportunities.

"We have had, and continue to have, discussions with certain acquisition candidates in this regard, and are continuing to aggressively pursue establishing a significant position in this sector of our industry," Hirschfeld said.
